analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow, patch, documentation and metadata units. release-swift.yml:119-155 removes master/manual dev publication, forces the dev validation lane to validation_only=true, and excludes validation dispatches from staging. Production's tag predicate remains unchanged (164-166); its dispatch predicate now excludes validation. No concrete security regression is established in this caller. A validation dispatch on a tag can still select both dev and prod predicates; integration should reconcile this with resolver rejection and their shared concurrency group, rather than infer publication from the predicates alone.
The unchanged release-provider.yml excerpt binds downloads to artifact ID, digest and signing run (1173-1184), gates publication on successful dependencies and publish=true (1088-1089), serializes publication per environment, and conditionally supplies prod/staging registration and storage credentials (1119-1151). Helper enforcement is not shown here.
New changelogs (dev-branch-builds-dev.md:4-5; master-publishes-staging-only.md:6-7) and docs/developer/test.md:1048-1078 describe expansion from ad-hoc dev builds to Developer-ID-signed dev artifacts. These claims are not implementation proof. Integration must examine the dev caller, master-owned source gate, resolver, signing job and publication helpers to verify dev source cannot alter trusted secret-bearing execution, cross environments, or bypass artifact/build qualification. Relevant assets/threats are A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-043 and T-054, including the fan-helper identity contract (T-045). Signing and notarization alone do not establish serving authorization or runtime secrecy (T-052/T-056). No supplied change directly modifies prompt encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing, or inference admission. This is a bounded source pass; the newly documented signing trust expansion remains material pending cross-file review.
